name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that overlays the dark theme’s text and background in real time as the user types. This guarantees readability before submission without slowing down the workflow. The trade-off is a small performance hit from constant color analysis, but it’s worth it to prevent unreadable text from ever reaching the final screen.

name: Pane
text: The live contrast checker risks training users to ignore the problem after the first few corrections—once they see it "works," they’ll stop checking. A better alternative is a pre-submission warning that forces acknowledgment of contrast issues before allowing the user to proceed. Settle it by testing both: measure how often users override the live checker versus how many submit with poor contrast despite the warning.

name: Facet
text:
Ship the pre-submission contrast validator that blocks unreadable submissions until fixed. It forces users to address contrast issues before moving forward, eliminating the risk of training them to ignore warnings. The trade-off is a slight friction in workflow, but it guarantees readability at submission time—no live overlay can match the certainty of a hard stop.

text: Pane: The pre-submission block risks user drop-off—users won’t tolerate being locked out mid-task. A better alternative is a live contrast checker that *also* logs unresolved issues for post-submission review, balancing safety with workflow.
